common_name: Sonic Bloom Pink Weigela (Reblooming Hot-Pink Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; strongest rebloom and best flower color develop with at least six hours of direct sun a day.

directions: Sonic Bloom Pink was the original introduction in the Sonic Bloom series, opening in a heavy flush of hot-pink, trumpet-shaped flowers in May and then continuing to rebloom on new growth in waves through summer and into fall without any deadheading required. Its full-size, upright-arching habit gives it a more traditional weigela presence in the border compared to the compact Sonic Bloom Pearl and Sonic Bloom Punch selections bred later in the series. Prune lightly right after the main spring flush if shaping is wanted, since heavy or late pruning removes the new growth that carries the later rebloom, and give it full sun and well-drained soil for the strongest performance.
sources: Proven Winners - Sonic Bloom Pink weigela notes

common_name: Sonic Bloom Wine Weigela (Reblooming Purple-Foliage Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun for the deepest foliage color and the most reliable rebloom.

directions: Sonic Bloom Wine pairs the repeat-flowering habit of the Sonic Bloom series with green foliage strongly tinted burgundy, giving the plant ongoing color interest between the bubblegum-pink flower flushes that appear from spring through summer. Like its Sonic Bloom siblings it blooms on both old and new wood, so a heavy spring flush is followed by continued waves of bloom into fall without deadheading. It needs only light pruning immediately after the main spring flowering to maintain shape, and is otherwise adaptable to a range of well-drained garden soils.
sources: Proven Winners - Sonic Bloom Wine weigela notes

common_name: Sonic Bloom Punch Weigela (Compact Reblooming Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; a slow-release shrub fertilizer applied in early spring supports the heaviest bloom.

directions: Sonic Bloom Punch is a more compact, wider-than-tall member of the Sonic Bloom series, covering itself in rich punch-pink, trumpet-shaped flowers in a heavy spring flush before taking a brief early-summer rest and then reblooming steadily through late summer into fall. Its lower, spreading habit fits smaller borders and foundation plantings where the larger Sonic Bloom Pink or Sonic Bloom Wine would need more room. Prune lightly right after the spring flush if needed, since little pruning is required to keep the plant full and well-shaped.
sources: Proven Winners - Sonic Bloom Punch weigela notes

common_name: Sonic Bloom Pure Pink Weigela (Reblooming Clear-Pink Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun for the strongest, cleanest flower color and best rebloom.

directions: Sonic Bloom Pure Pink carries clear, uniform pink flowers rather than the deeper or two-tone shades of other Sonic Bloom siblings, opening in a strong late-spring flush and then, after a brief rest, sending up further waves of bloom through summer to frost. It is a continuous rebloomer that flowers on both old and new wood, keeping hummingbirds visiting for a much longer season than single-flush weigela cultivars. Prune right after the spring bloom if shaping is wanted, and once the shrub is mature, remove one to three of the oldest, heaviest stems each year to keep new growth vigorous and the plant full.
sources: Proven Winners - Sonic Bloom Pure Pink weigela notes

common_name: Wine and Spirits Weigela (Black-Purple Foliage White-Pink Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; foliage darkens most in strong sun, though light shade is tolerated in hot climates.

directions: Wine and Spirits stands out among the dark-leaved weigela cultivars for foliage that deepens to an almost black-purple, providing a dramatic backdrop for its bicolor flowers, which open white and are edged and flushed with reddish pink in late spring through early summer. It blooms on old wood in a single strong flush rather than reblooming through summer like the Sonic Bloom series, so any shaping should be done immediately afterward to avoid removing next year's buds. It tolerates average garden soil well once established and needs little routine care beyond that timely pruning.
sources: Proven Winners - Wine & Spirits weigela notes

common_name: Midnight Wine Shine Weigela (Glossy Dwarf Purple-Foliage Weigela)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; the glossy foliage holds its richest color and luster with at least six hours of direct sun.

directions: Midnight Wine Shine is a newer, glossier-leaved improvement on the original Midnight Wine, holding deep purple foliage with a notably high-gloss sheen from spring through fall on a low, dense, spreading mound under a foot and a half tall. Soft pink, trumpet-shaped flowers appear in a single spring flush on old wood, drawing bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds, and its naturally deer- and rabbit-resistant foliage makes it a dependable small-space edging or container plant. Prune only right after flowering if shaping is needed, since later pruning removes the following year's flower buds, and it otherwise needs little maintenance once established in well-drained soil.
sources: Proven Winners - Midnight Wine Shine weigela notes
